title: Special Order
text: As I stepped inside the Monster Merchant’s tent alongside my Father—who had clenched his fist in front of his chest as if summoning his courage—the Monster Merchant came out to greet us.
“Well, well, Heroes, thank you so much for visiting our shop. Yes.”
“Ah, so? Can you get the slave we requested?”
“Yes, yes. Fortunately, a fellow merchant had just purchased one, so I was able to prepare it right away. Yes.”
With that, the Monster Merchant ordered one of his subordinates to bring over a piglet that looked familiar.
“Oink, oink, oink!”
The piglet—presumably Keel—was struggling as if in protest. To be honest, I can’t really tell for sure since I’ve only ever seen Keel as a puppy. If he were a puppy, we could even talk…
“Is this one all right? Yes.”
“Ah, ah… So, how much?”
“Taking into account the Shield Hero’s character, let’s settle on 45 silver coins, including the slave registration ceremony. Yes.”
Father’s eyes are darting around slightly, and he’s holding his breath. That’s right. I whisper to Father.

“Father. You should also ask him to give you a little bit of the ink used for slave registration while you’re at it. With that material, you can craft weapons that boost a slave’s abilities and growth stats.”
I’ve never actually commanded a slave myself, but I have crafted spears using ink as a material. Well, I suppose my collection isn’t as extensive as Father’s, though.
“U-uh-huh.”
Father takes a step forward and walks toward the monster merchant. He adopted a high-handed attitude before speaking.
“Hmm… So this is Keel, is it?”
“Bububububu-!”
At that moment, Keel…
‘What the hell! You’re planning to abuse me again, aren’t you! I’m not losing this, no way!’
…was saying something defiant like that, Father told me.
“It seems he has a bit of a temper, but are you really sure this is okay? Yes.”

Just to be safe, the monster merchant asked again, but Father showed a slight flicker of panic—one that only I could detect. Of course, without making any mistakes that might give himself away to the monster merchant, Father replied.
“This kind of temperament makes training him more fun. That’s what a slave is all about, isn’t it?”
The monster merchant nodded excitedly at Father’s response.
“As expected of the Great Shield Hero! Then I’ll proceed with the slave registration. Yes!”
“Ah, while you’re at it, hand me a little of the ink used for slave registration. I’ll use it as material for the Hero’s weapon.”
“Understood. Yes!”

He’s quite generous, isn’t he? It’s a world of difference from how it was with me. Even I, watching it unfold right before my eyes, can’t figure out exactly how to get this Monster Merchant to go the extra mile. Is speaking in a high-handed manner the key? Father must be on the same wavelength as this monster merchant when it comes to negotiations.

The monster merchant transferred the ink for the slave registration into a small dish and explained to Father that he needed to add blood for the registration. Father peeled off the scab from the wound he’d made yesterday when registering Sakura-chan and let his blood drip into the ink. Then, one of the monster merchant’s subordinates pinned down a pig—presumably Keel—to register the slave mark.
“Ooogggh!”

The pig—presumably Keel—screamed in pain during the registration. It looked a bit like a slaughter, but Keel stopped squealing partway through, as if trying to endure the pain. Even in this state, she’s still Big Sister’s fellow townswoman.
“Oink… oink…”
Breathing heavily, Keel’s registration was complete. Father seemed to be checking various things with his eyes, just as he did during the monster mark registration.
“Well then… I suppose we’re done here.”
With a jingle of coins, Father handed some silver coins to the Monster Merchant and looked down at Keel.
“Now then, I’m going to put you to good use from here on out. Do your best to survive.”
“Buh!”
Keel is glaring at my Father with hostility, but I wonder how long that’ll last? Thinking about Keel’s future, it’ll be interesting to see just how attached he becomes, given Father’s personality.
“See ya. I’ll come back when I need something.”
“We look forward to your next visit. Yes, sir.”
Father turned around and forcefully pulled Keel by the hand.
“Come on, let’s go.”
“Yes, sir!”
I followed Father’s retreating figure and stepped out of the tent.
“‘Piyo!’”
Yuki-chan and the others were waiting outside the tent to greet me.
“I’m home.”
“‘Piyo!’”
“I’m so glad you were such good girls while I was away.”

I petted Yuki-chan and the others before giving them a hug. Yuki-chan and the others are entering their growth spurt, and their bellies are rumbling loudly. Seeing this, Keel seems to be blinking in surprise. But he quickly looked away.
“What should we do now…? Should Motoyasu-kun take this one out to level up?”
“That sounds about right.”

Anyway, to level up Sakura-chan, I’ll have to wait until nightfall again today, acting like nothing’s up. It’d be a problem if we were spotted hanging out together too much. Still, I have no idea what Keel is saying. It’s also true that things would be a real hassle if Yuki-chan and the others couldn’t speak.
“Father. I can’t understand pig language, so right now, I can’t take care of Keel.”
“Come to think of it, you often insult women by calling them pigs… Motoyasu-kun, is there a reason for that?”
“A pig is a pig. It’s a despicable, self-centered, lowly creature that oinks and squeals.”
“Huh… So, Motoyasu-kun, for whatever reason, women look like pigs to you. Is it the loop’s influence? Wait—this kid’s a girl!?”
“Oink!?”
Just as I thought Keel was teasing Yuki-chan and the others, she suddenly flinched and turned her face toward Father.
“I thought being a pretty boy might make him better at sales, but this kid’s a girl… Hmm…”
“Oink! Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink!”
It looks like Keel is clenching his fist in protest. I don’t know anything about that. We work like workhorses for Father! That’s the job of us, his retainers.
“Well… if that’s how she feels, isn’t that fine? I look forward to working with you from now on.”
“O-oink…?”
Keel tilted her head at Father’s words and looked completely dumbfounded. It’s a pig’s reaction, but I kind of get it. It’s that obvious from her expression.
“Alright, then for the time being, I’ll be Keel-chan’s—”
“Oink!”
“—’ll take care of Keel-chan, so Motoyasu, please look after Sakura-chan. I’m going to try leveling up a bit with Kou and Keel.”
“Understood.”
“We’ll need gear for that, won’t we?”

Ah, that’s right. First, we need to go to the weapon shop and buy the gear Keel needs. In this regard, it’s absolutely wonderful that equipment isn’t that important in Filolial-sama. Admittedly, buying gear for a pig is hard to wrap my head around, but since it’s Father’s idea, I won’t complain.
When we went to the weapon shop, the shopkeeper saw Father and Keel and put his finger to the wrinkle between his eyebrows, deep in thought.
“An-chan…”
“No, it’s not my fault! Please don’t look at me like that!”
Father is frantically trying to persuade the shopkeeper. It seems the old man is lamenting the fact that he’s bought a pig… no, wait—a slave.
“Is it the country’s fault, or has An-chan become tainted…?”
“I’ll admit the country’s to blame, but I’m not tainted at all! There are all sorts of reasons for this!”
“Sigh… Well, I’ll let it slide this time. What brings you here today?”
My father-in-law shifted his gaze briefly to Keel.
“I’d like you to pick out some decent gear for this kid. We’ll be fighting side by side from now on.”
“Oink!?”
My father knelt down, met Keel’s gaze, and said,
“I haven’t introduced myself yet, have I? My name is Naofumi Iwatani. I was summoned to this world as the Shield Hero.”
